disposition_reason: Table 1 prints mean (minimum-maximum) total arsenic, mercury, copper and lead (µg/g dry weight, AAS) in five market fruits, including imported apples.

study.design: Market basket survey of five fruits
study.origin: Locally supplied, except apples imported largely from South Africa
study.market: Eke Awka market, Awka, Anambra State, Nigeria
study.method: Oven drying at 55 °C, microwave HNO3 digestion, AAS at a commercial laboratory
study.qa: NIST SRM 1515 apple leaves, 1575a pine needles, 1568a rice flour; mean recoveries 75-98.5%

findings.group: Eke Awka market, Awka, Anambra State
findings.notes: Mean (minimum-maximum) in µg/g dry weight; Methods say ten samples purchased per fruit, figure legends say n = 3; values below detection were set to 0 before statistics. Arsenic levels of 20-97 µg/g dry weight are far above typical fruit levels.

unresolved: Wet-weight values appear only in Figures 2-5 (bar charts) and were not read; moisture contents are printed (guava 80.8%, apple 84%, pineapple 87%, orange 87%, pawpaw 85.5%) but no wet-weight values were computed here.
Methyl mercury in Figure 3 is derived by assuming 83% of total mercury; not extracted.
Sample count conflict: ten samples purchased per fruit (Methods) vs n = 3 (figure legends).
Orange and pawpaw arsenic means equal their maxima with minima <0.001; flagged.
Abstract lead range (<0.001-0.03±0.05) does not match Table 1 guava lead 0.05 (0.03-0.07).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Codex guideline levels used for comparison, as cited
regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 0.50, Hg 0.10, Cu 2.00, Pb 0.10 µg/g wet weight
